name: Carte de résident (10-year permanent residence)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 5 years of uninterrupted regular residence in France, with limited exceptions for certain family/refugee categories.
This requires French at CEFR B1.
requirements.fix_path: Prepare for and pass an approved test at B1.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires having completed the Contrat d'Intégration Républicaine (CIR) obligations undertaken at the start of residence, and demonstrated republican integration more broadly.

evidence_required.document: TCF or DELF certificate at B1

outcome.duration_length: indefinite; the physical card is renewed every 10 years

sources.title: Légifrance — CESEDA, carte de résident provisions
Légifrance — Loi n° 2024-42 du 26 janvier 2024 (B1 language requirement for carte de résident)

notes: France's ILR-equivalent hub route, same structural role as uk_ilr, de_niederlassungserlaubnis, nl_permanent_residence, pt_permanent_residence, and es_permanent_residence. Distinct from the general EU long-term residence permit in some technical respects (carte de résident is the French national implementation, with an EU long-term-resident variant also available with similar conditions) — modeled as a single route here, consistent with the scope simplification applied to the equivalent hub routes in Netherlands, Portugal, and Spain. citizenship_after_months is 0 since holding this card is what makes naturalisation possible at 0 additional months per fr_naturalisation's own 60-month figure being measured from initial residence, not from carte de résident grant — the two clocks run in parallel from the same starting point rather than stacking sequentially, a genuine structural difference from Portugal's system (where PR and citizenship clocks are explicitly sequential and stack). B1 French requirement here sits below the B2 required for citizenship itself — part of the tiered A2/B1/B2 ladder (pluriannual card / carte de résident / naturalisation) confirmed during this research pass, worth surfacing as a coherent progressive system rather than three unrelated figures.
